title: Crowned with Confidence: Racial Socialization and the Disruption of Racial Stigma in Black Girlhood
content: Racial stigma reflects internalized beliefs about Black people that can shape identity development and psychological wellbeing. Research on the impact of daily racial dis-crimination on Black girls’ development of racial stigma beliefs is scarce. The current study examined Black girls (Mage = 14, N = 118) reports of racial discrimination experiences and the association on racial stigma beliefs (i.e., endorsing negative stereotypes about Black Americans). The protective role of racial socialization strategies was also examined. Using a hierarchical regression analysis, the findings revealed that higher levels of racial discrimination was associated with higher levels of racial stigma. Spiritual and religious coping and racial awareness teaching were associated with lower levels of racial stigma. The interaction effects indicated that Black girls who reported higher levels of daily racial discrimination and lower levels of cultural pride reinforcement were more likely to endorse negative stereotypes about Black people.
